dedupe_keys.name: ipc acute food insecurity country data population by ipc phase current and projected

description: This dataset contains the population figures behind the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, the common scale used by governments, UN agencies and NGOs to grade acute food insecurity from phase 1 (minimal) to phase 5 (catastrophe or famine). The National IPC Technical Working Groups produce the analyses, the IPC Global Support Unit compiles them, and the tables are published on the Humanitarian Data Exchange and through the IPC's own API. Coverage is every country and analysis area with an IPC acute analysis since 2017, including projected periods reaching into 2027, with the number and share of people in each phase for each area and analysis period. National totals rest on official population estimates. Files are free CSV downloads released under a public-domain (CC0) dedication and refreshed as new analyses are published; the IPC API adds area geometries for mapping. Caveats: analyses are episodic and cover only countries that request them, area units change between analyses, projected figures are scenarios, not observations, and West and Central African countries mostly use the Cadre Harmonise instead. Simulation uses: setting baseline food insecurity for food supply disruption and emergency response scenarios, prioritising humanitarian logistics, and validating early-warning or forecasting models. Related records: the Cadre Harmonise data (data-cadre-harmonise-west-central-africa) cover West Africa, FEWS NET (data-fews-net-data-explorer) gives complementary outlooks, and OpenRelief (model-openrelief) forecasts IPC phases.
